PixelArtistry · Settings (low-poly)
widgets_values:
### Low-poly + baking

**LODTailor (A):** `target_tris` 20–30k for characters, 500–1,000 for props. `relative_voxel_size` 0.0015 for organic shapes, 0.05 for hard-surface (keeps sharper edges). More `passes` = better result, but slower.

**Bake Forger (B):** all maps at 4096 – set the `*_resolution` values to 2048 or 8192 if you like. `tight_cage_extrusion_factor`: 0.0019 for characters, 0.019 for hard-surface – raise it if white patches appear on the low-poly.

**Fast Merge (C):** welds duplicate vertices and tiny gaps of the baked low-poly in `TEXTURE_SAFE` mode, so the UVs stay intact. If it can't close the mesh, it passes the file through unchanged. No Blender needed.

**Checking in Blender:** import the textured low-poly with **Merge Vertices** ticked. A GLB can't give one vertex two UV coordinates, so UV seams otherwise show up as open edges.

**Blender:** LODTailor and Bake Forger read the path from the *Blender path* node. Use a clean Blender without add-ons (portable install) – add-ons like Auto-Rig Pro can break headless runs.

**Output:** `output/3d/PixelArtistry_hi3d_lowpoly_*.glb` – the baked game-ready asset.

nodes.title: PixelArtistry · Start here
widgets_values:
# PixelArtistry · Hi3D 04 · Image → Low-poly Game Character (TRELLIS.2 + Hi3D + UltraTex)

## Before the first run: this workflow needs two installs

1. **Hi3D** – `Install-Hi3D.bat` from https://github.com/pixelartistry/PixelArtistry-Hi3D
2. **Animated-Characters** – the installer from https://github.com/pixelartistry/PixelArtistry-Animated-Characters
   It brings LODTailor, Bake Forger, Fast Merge, Memory Cleaner, ComfyUI-GGUF and **MostAadTech's low-VRAM UltraTex nodes** (their names start with `UTX`), with their models.

**Red nodes, 12 unknown `UTX…` nodes, or the error `Node 'ID #353' has no class_type`?** MostAadTech's UltraTex nodes are missing. Close ComfyUI, run the Animated-Characters installer, start ComfyUI again. ComfyUI Manager can't install them ("Unknown pack"), and the standard UltraTex install is not enough: it brings visualbruno's nodes, this workflow uses MostAadTech's.

---

**Texture stage is OFF.** The TRELLIS/Pixal3D texture nodes are muted (grey), because UltraTex paints colour and metal/roughness anyway. Bake Forger only bakes the normal map. Saves a few minutes and about 100 MB per run. To get the old textured high-poly back, unmute the grey nodes and reconnect *Apply textures* → *High-poly → GLB* and *Vertex colors* → *Unwrap UVs (low-poly)*.

One run: TRELLIS.2 (1024) → **Hi3D 512 > 1024** detail → 12k low-poly → **Bake Forger** (normal map) → **UltraTex (MostAadTech, GGUF)** paints albedo + metallic/roughness on the same UVs → **Apply Materials** merges both → `output/3d/PixelArtistry_hi3d_final_*.glb`.

UltraTex: 4 steps (fast; set 25 on both Generate nodes for final quality), 12 albedo views incl. guided 45° pass, 2048 textures, UV mode keep_existing.

---

# PixelArtistry · Image → Game-Ready 3D Asset

Free & local ComfyUI workflow by **PixelArtistry**.

## How to use
1. Load your image in **Load Image** (green group).
2. Set your Blender path once in **Blender path** (group 1).
3. Choose the model with **Boolean (Switch to Trellis2)**: `false` = Pixal3D, `true` = Trellis.2
4. Set **LODTailor (A)** `target_tris`: 20–30k for characters, 500–1,000 for props.
5. Press **Run**.

## What happens
TRELLIS.2 generates the shape → **Hi3D** adds the detail (`PixelArtistry_hi3d_detail_1024`) → **LODTailor** builds the low-poly → **Bake Forger** bakes the Hi3D detail into its normal map → **Fast Merge** welds duplicate vertices without breaking the UVs (`PixelArtistry_hi3d_lowpoly`).

Both files land in `ComfyUI/output/3d/`.

## PixelArtistry
- Website: https://pixel-artistry.com
- YouTube: [youtube.com/@PixelArtistry_](https://www.youtube.com/@PixelArtistry_)
- X: https://x.com/philippsieben
- Newsletter FutureFrames: https://pixel-artistry.com/newsletter

## Built with MostAadTech's nodes
The low-poly and baking steps in this workflow run on free, open-source ComfyUI nodes by **MostAadTech**. He spent over a month building them and was a huge help while these workflows were made – please show him some love:

- **Memory Cleaner** – frees VRAM between the heavy steps
- **LODTailor** – builds the lighter or low-poly mesh in Blender
- **Bake Forger** – bakes the high-poly maps onto the low-poly
- **Fast Merge** – welds duplicate vertices for a clean final file

**Follow & support MostAadTech**

UltraTex Modular FAST v0.2.3 — view resolution and 6/12-view count are controlled ONLY on Generate. Prepare owns UVs and reference mask. IMPORTANT: for BiRefNet, mask_polarity=foreground. nodes.title: Read me · Models

widgets_values:
## 3 · Prepare
Renders the normal views and lines your reference up with the front camera.

**Check the three previews before a long run:**
- **Normal views:** your mesh from all sides.
- **Aligned reference:** the object should fill the silhouette **edge to edge**.
- **Aligned mask:** white object on black.

Small or shifted? Check `mask_polarity`: **foreground** for BiRefNet, **background** if you use Load Image's own MASK instead.
nodes.title: Read me · Prepare

widgets_values:
## 4 · Generate views
**All quality and speed settings live on the two Generate nodes.**

| Setting | Albedo | MR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_resolution` | **1024** | 1024 | 6 GB: 1024 · 8 GB: up to 1536–2048 |
| `view_count` | **12** | **6** | 12 = 6 + a guided 45° pass |
| `steps` | **4** | 4 | dev: 4 is enough, 8 is better |
| `extra_angle_mode` | guided | – | 45° pass starts from pass 1 |

- **Same seed** on both Generate nodes.
- **Steps are the speed lever.** Time scales with steps. Compare 4 / 8 / 25 on your asset and judge the back and sides, not just the front.
- MR maps are low-detail, so **6 views** are enough there.
- `tiled_decode` **on** for low VRAM.
nodes.title: Read me · Generate

widgets_values:
## 5 · Bake & save
Bakes albedo and MR views onto the **one shared UV layout**. Saves to `output/ultratex/`:
- textured **GLB** (+ Preview 3D)
- **base color**, **roughness** and **metallic** maps as separate PNGs

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `texture_size` | 2048 (4096 for hero assets, same VRAM, slower bake) |
| `fill_unseen` | on: estimates hidden areas (no new detail) |
| `blend_mode` | detail_preserving |
| `repair_mode` | normal_aware_surface |

Faceted face? Try `normal_mode = preserve` vs `smooth` in Prepare.

widgets_values:
## 0 · Hi3D detail (AeroX, 6 GB)

TRELLIS.2 builds the shape at 1024, then **Hi3D** adds the fine detail before the low-poly bake.

1. **Free VRAM** after TRELLIS.2
2. **Remesh twice** (solid, fill 20): AeroX's fix for broken thin parts
3. **Hi3D 512 > 1024**, conditioned on your input image
4. The 1024 mesh goes straight to the low-poly + bake: its detail ends up in the **normal map**. UltraTex then paints the low-poly.

**Why no 1536 pass?** A 2K normal map can't hold more detail than the 1024 mesh already has, and the 1536 pass doubles the time and the memory. For a high-poly render or sculpt, use workflow 01 (512 > 1024 > 1536).

Saved: `3d/PixelArtistry_hi3d_detail_1024`. 6-8 GB: int8, 12 GB+: fp16 also works.

nodes.title: 1 · Bake source
widgets_values:
## 1 · Bake source: the Hi3D mesh, as it is

The older workflow made the high-poly **watertight** first (Quad Reconstruct > WTiVo > LODTailor 6M), because raw TRELLIS.2 meshes are full of holes. **With Hi3D that step is not needed:**

- Hi3D's mesh already has **0 open holes**.
- **LODTailor (A)** rebuilds the low-poly with a voxel remesh, so the game mesh comes out closed anyway.
- **Bake Forger** only reads the surface of the high-poly to bake the normal map. It doesn't need a watertight mesh.

Skipping it saves several minutes and a lot of memory: WTiVo on a Hi3D mesh needs far more system RAM than anything else in this workflow.

**You only need watertight for 3D printing.** For that, run the saved Hi3D mesh through the *Watertight High-Poly* workflow afterwards.

**Blender path:** set it once in the node on the left. LODTailor and Bake Forger use it.
